This was actually an issue :) assigned :)

The problem in the stock bazel source, with new_local_repository, is that there is no WORKSPACE file, which is what [LocalRepositoryLookupFunction](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/LocalRepositoryLookupFunction.java) is using to check for the presence of a local repository. The WORKSPACE file generated by [NewLocalRepositoryRule](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/repository/NewLocalRepositoryRule.java) is located at:
```
[output_base]/external/com_google_protobuf/WORKSPACE
```
but the actual query is looking at the directory path
```
[bazel_dir]/third_party/protobuf/3.0.0/WORKSPACE
```
so there is no match.

There's not an easy way to solve this that I know of.

If we change com_google_protobuf to a local_repository, as the 'git diff' seems to indicate, there is still no WORKSPACE present in [bazel_dir]/third_party/protobuf/3.0.0/, so it is not detected as a local repository.

Also, the way LocalRepositoryLookupFunction tests for local_repositories is brittle, specifically it's relying on [PathFragment](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/vfs/PathFragment.java).equals() to check if paths match, and that is confused by the leading "./" in the path of com_google_protobuf.

If I fix the path, and also add an empty WORKSPACE, then LocalRepositoryLookupFunction detects the repository and filters out the references to //third_party/protobuf/3.0.0.

Clone https://github.com/katre/bazel/tree/i2811-query-oddness to see the changes I made.

Action items:
1. File an issue on [LocalRepositoryRule](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/rules/repository/LocalRepositoryRule.java) to give an error if there is no WORKSPACE file.
2. File an issue on PathFragment.equals to properly handle relative paths starting with "./" or "../". OR forbid those in the path attribute of repositories.
3. Why do we have two repositories, com_google_protobuf and com_google_protobuf_java, pointing to the same directory? If we need both names, can

issue.title: LocalRepositoryRule should report an error if there is no WORKSPACE file

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
If a local_repository is defined but there is no WORKSPACE file in the directory, report an error. Specifically, Bazel should not attempt to create one (as it does for NewLocalRepositoryRule) because the WORKSPACE needs to be in the actual package directory, not solely in the output_base/external directory.

Related to #2811.

issue.title: PathFragment.equals should properly handle paths that are different but refer to the same directory

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
Currently, [PathFragment.equals](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/vfs/PathFragment.java#L762) simply checks that the paths are identical, but does not handle paths containing "./" or "../" segments. PathFragment should either handle this case, or explicitly not support such a case and provide an alternative that does.

Expected behavior:
```java
PathFragment frag1 = PathFragment.create("foo");
PathFragment frag2 = PathFragment.create("./foo");
frag1.equals(frag2) == false; // Should be true
```

Related to #2811.

issue.title: Bazel does not properly handle nested workspaces from vendorized dependencies

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem:

Bazel does not properly handle nested workspaces from vendorized dependencies.
* Bazel targets within dependencies are evaluated relative to the containing workspace. This causes commands to work correctly when run from within the vendorized dependency, but to fail when run in from the parent workspace.
* Dependencies have no way to describe their licensing at a workspace-level, so modifications must be made to BUILD files throughout the vendorized dependency to add license information.

### Minimal example:

https://github.com/chpatton013/bad_dependency
```
%> tree
.
├── BUILD
├── WORKSPACE
└── dependency
    ├── BUILD
    ├── WORKSPACE
    └── build.bzl
```

From `//dependency`, run `bazel build ...`. Build is successful.
```
%> bazel build ...
INFO: Found 0 targets...
INFO: Elapsed time: 0.151s, Critical Path: 0.00s
```

From `//`, run `bazel build ...`. Build is unsucessful.
```
%> bazel build ...
ERROR: package contains errors: dependency.
ERROR: error loading package 'dependency': Extension file not found. Unable to load file '//:build.bzl': file doesn't exist or isn't a file.
INFO: Elapsed time: 0.148s
```

### Environment info
* Operating System: Ubuntu
* Bazel version (output of `bazel info release`): 0.4.3
* If `bazel info release` returns "development version" or "(@non-git)", please tell us what source tree you compiled Bazel from; git commit hash is appreciated (`git rev-parse HEAD`): release 0.4.3-2017-01-23 (@065e9ef)
